full_judgment:
5. Mr. M.A. Karim, the learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the plaintiff-petitioner has first submitted that having regard to the fact that the suit lands along with other lands of the two Hebas Ext. A and A (1) dated 17th Magh, 1255 B.S. and 24th Poush, 1274 B.S. respectively and of Ext. 1, the khatian having been described as Cheragi, according to him, dedicated property in `Rahelillah' or public wakf properties the learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law apparent on the face of record in holding that the claim of the plaintiff that Jangli Bibi dedicated the properties in `Rahelillah Wakf' is not borne out by any direct evidence and thus he caused failure of justice. He has next submitted that the trial court has interpreted Ext. A, the Hebanama as a whole and decreed the suit but the learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law in holding that the tank is not a `rahelillah' or a public wakf property inasmuch as that he has come to his finding as to the character of the properties upon interpretation of some words of the deed instead of reading the document as a whole, and thus has caused a failure of justice. He has further submitted that the stipulations in Exts 'A' and A (I), the two heba deeds, having provided that out of the income of the properties i.e. including the suit tank, the mosque will be maintained, Imam its will be appointed and light will be provided in the mosque, undoubtedly show the character of the properties but the learned Additional District Judge upon an apparent, error of law held the tank to be secular property. He has further submitted that on the face of the evidence that the tank had been used since time immemorial by the 'musallis' of the mosque for ablution for prayers, the learned Additional District Judge committed an error in holding that tank is not a public wakf. The learned Advocate has next submitted having regard to the fact that the judgment and decree of Title Suit No. 273 of 1920 clearly proved that Lutfunnessa Bibi possessed the suit tank adjacent to mosque as Mutwalli, the learned Additional District Judge committed an error of law apparent on the face of the record in holding that there is nothing in the decree to show that Lutfunnessa claimed herself as Mutwalli of the mosque, and this has caused a serious failure of justice and his decision is liable to be set aside. 

 8. As regards the ownership of the properties of taluk No. 2 to which the suit tank appertains, there is no dispute. The present dispute in this Rule turns round the question whether the court of appeal below committed any error of law apparent on the face of the record in holding that the tank is not a public wakf. The plaintiff has alleged that the tank was excavated on plot No. 137 by Jangli Bibi and dedicated in `Rahelillah' for the purpose of ablution of the 'musallis' before prayers and maintenance of the mosque. There is no express evidence of dedication of the tank in `Rahelillah. In the absence of any direct evidence of dedication the plaintiff has relied upon the recitals in the two deeds of heba, Ext. A and A (1) referred to above, the khatian Ext. 1 and the judgment and decree of Title Suit No.161 of 1974. The learned Additional District Judge on consideration of these documents has held that there is no evidence of dedication of the tank in 'rehelillah or appointment of Amir Kazi as Mutwalli of the proper-ties. He has further held that Jangli Bibi gifted the property in favour of Amir Kazi who became the absolute owner but an obligation was created by the document to the effect that the donee would maintain the mosque and provide oil and light in the mosque or in other words the donee would spend a portion of the income of the property for the maintenance of the mosque. 

 9. Let me consider whether the learned Additional District Judge committed any error of law on the face of the record in holding that there was no evidence of dedication of the tank in 'rehelillah' or in other words, any wakf with respect to the suit tank was made by Jangli Bibi, the admitted owner of the tank. Although in Exts A and A (1) the two deeds of Heba, the properties have been described as cheragi, and Ext. 'C' the khatian has described the tenure as cheragi of Amir Kali, should the description of the properties as cheragi in these documents prove that the properties were dedicated to Allah creating a valid wakf for maintenance of the mosque, payment of the salary of the Imam and lighting of the mosque. There is no direct evidence that there was any dedication of the properties to Allah by creating of wakf. The learned Additional District Judge on consideration of the recitals of the two documents was of the view that there was no dedication of the properties in `rahelillah' or that there has been no dedication of the properties creating any Wald. According to the learned Additional District Judge the tank along with other properties were gifted by the donors of the Hebas to the respective domes for enjoyment from generation to generation with an obligation to apply same income out of them to provide light in the mosque and to maintain it by appointing an Imam. In my view the recitals in both the deeds of Heba created absolute transfers to the domes for their enjoyment from generation to generation but with an obligation to maintain the mosque. The recitals in the two deeds of heba did not create any dedication of the properties in `rahelillah'. The recitals, however, indicate that out of the income of the properties, presently the tank, maintenance of the mosque, appointment of an Imam and providing lights in the mosque was to be made by the domes. In my view the learned Additional District Judge committed no error of law apparent on the face of the record in holding that there has been no dedication of the tank in `rahelillah' for the maintenance of the mosque or for providing lights therein.
